core.title: Advance decomposition only through per-candidate keep/pivot/kill verdicts
core.given: A decomposition session where the planner proposes candidates at the decomposition granularities the profile names (artifact-authoring kinds and reasoning kinds).
core.when: The planner would advance past a candidate or act on it.
core.then: Advance each candidate only on the operator's individual keep, pivot or kill verdict for that candidate.
prefer: Pivot: apply the operator's named modification, then re-confirm.
Kill: reject; if all candidates at a granularity are killed, re-propose.
Write an artifact only after a keep at an artifact-authoring (final) granularity, i.e. one of the plan-artifact kinds in the profile.
Reasoning granularities are real candidates, but a keep records the decision and writes no artifact.
avoid: Advancing a candidate that has no individual verdict (several individually assigned verdicts may be delivered together).
Writing an artifact before a final-granularity keep, or a pivot before re-confirmation.
Erroring on a kept reasoning-level candidate, or recording kill when the operator kept it.
core.why: Per-unit verdicts keep the operator in control and recorded decisions truthful; only final granularities author an artifact.
evidence: Each authored artifact traces to a recorded keep verdict (or a re-confirmed pivot) on that candidate at a final granularity.
Kept reasoning-granularity candidates appear as recorded decisions with no artifact and no error from the authoring step.
All-killed granularities are followed by a re-proposal, not by an artifact.
Every advanced candidate has its own recorded verdict.
verification: The check treats as final exactly the candidate kinds the profile lists as plan-artifact kinds, and as reasoning the kinds the profile lists as reasoning decomposition kinds; verdicts are per candidate even when several individually assigned verdicts are delivered together.
The check must not let the authoring step fail on a kept reasoning-granularity candidate, and kill must not be the only verdict that leaves a session able to author artifacts (a regression guard).

Operator prose is interpreted as keep, pivot or kill to produce the recorded verdicts; the check verifies recorded verdicts against authored artifacts and recorded decisions, so that every advanced candidate and every authored artifact is supported by a recorded verdict.

fires: The planner proposes a candidate at an artifact-authoring granularity and is about to write its artifact.
The operator pivots a candidate with a named modification and the planner considers writing it without re-confirmation.
The operator kills every candidate at a granularity.
The operator keeps a candidate at a reasoning granularity.
doesNotFire: Editing an already-kept artifact outside a decomposition session (e.g. fixing a typo in an existing plan artifact).
Coder work implementing an already-planned artifact.
Reading or reviewing plans without proposing new candidates.

profileRequirements.meaning: The decomposition candidate kinds that author a plan artifact (the final granularities): an artifact is written only after a keep at one of these kinds, and their names are the task terms that signal decomposition work.
profileRequirements.bunValue: product capability, feature, DESIRED OUTCOME, user/system flow, flow router, contract, acceptance

profileRequirements.meaning: The plan decomposition levels that record a decision but author no artifact (the reasoning granularities): a keep on one of these writes no artifact and must not fail the authoring step, and their names are also task terms.

neutralityNotes: The decomposition-granularity taxonomy (which candidate kinds author artifacts versus record decisions) is stack data and comes entirely from the profile: roles.plan_artifact.kinds for the final granularities and roles.plan_hierarchy#decomposition_reasoning_kinds (plan decomposition levels that author no artifact) for the reasoning granularities. The ATDD-Bun authoring tool ('atdd author writer' / 'author dispatch') is referred to only functionally as the artifact-authoring step; its name and the #1929 regression reference stay in bunOnly. Planner, operator and coder are method-level agent roles rather than stack roles, so they remain in the core. Interpretation of operator prose as a verdict is a judged input (activation fact, llm_judged); the core does not prescribe where that interpretation happens, only that recorded verdicts support every advancement and authored artifact. bun.json declares no per-rule severity or disposition, so core:verification carries only the check's scope, its exclusions (verdicts delivered together) and the regression guard.
